name: Accounts
plan: S4 VARIANT 1: an adult who still holds a childhood Trump account contributes $7,000 a year of non-deductible money to it and converts that account alone to a Roth IRA with no income, despite $100,000 of pre-tax money in another traditional IRA (s.530A(h)(4) has no age limit).

tests.detail: No reading of s.530A more generous than its words was found, but the gain depends on scenario facts and on the objective: it is zero with no growth premium, with a deductible IRA, with the IRA already rolled into a plan, with equal rates, or with about $70,000 of untaxed money in the Trump account.

Adding 'For any taxable year beginning before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18,' to s.530A(h)(4) removes the plan and leaves all 15 baselines unchanged.
Removing either Trump-account move kills the plan; removing next-year halves it; removing every unused move, or allowing all 35, leaves +3,500.
Under the Code without s.530A nothing beats the baseline of 125,000.
Over every position reached, assets are conserved, pre-tax dollars are either still inside or taxed, basis never exceeds balance, and no limit is exceeded.

Plan and closed-gap replays pass the kernel by decide on the full state; a statement over all move sequences is proved by induction for a cut-down model whose agreement with the full closed step is checked by #eval only.
A Python script written from s.72(e)(8), s.408(d)(2)(C), s.408(o) and s.530A(h)(4) gives the same figures.
Notice 2025-68 states both halves of the plan (post-18 contributions under s.408(a)(1); non-aggregation 'at all times'); nothing closes it; no source found describing the combined plan.

divergences: Objective, not statute: the whole +$3,500 is the 25% premium on $14,000 of Roth money; with beta 0 the gain is 0.
Missing move: no roll-in of the ordinary IRA to an employer plan (s.408(d)(3)(A)(ii)), so the baseline omits the known way to reach the same result.
Scenario facts: iraDeductible false with has401k false (s.219(g) needs an active participant); if the deduction is allowed the plan adds nothing.
Scenario facts: the Trump account is empty; s.530A(d)(2) seed money and growth are untaxed and cut the gain by 5% of their amount.
Missing restriction: hasTA never ends, though the governing instrument may move the account to an ordinary IRA at 18 (Notice 2025-68 A-10) and a trustee may close an unfunded one (s.1.530A-1T(c)(6)).
Timing: the basis ratio is taken at the move, not at year end (s.408(d)(2)(C)); never more generous, no effect on this plan.
taAdult exists only for this plan and S3; with the plan's three move kinds the search is 14 positions.
The findings cite REG-117270-25, withdrawn 30 Sep 2026 (replaced by T.D. 10056 and CC-00226466-26).

authority.quote: a Trump account continues to be a Trump account after the growth period. ... an account initially established as a Trump account can never be aggregated with other individual retirement arrangements when allocating basis related to a distribution from either the Trump account or another individual retirement arrangement.

at all times, Trump accounts are disregarded for purposes of determining the portion of a distribution from a traditional individual retirement arrangement that is not a Trump account that is allocated to basis. The Treasury Department and the IRS anticipate issuing additional guidance with respect to this tax treatment for individual retirement arrangements in general.
during the growth period, the limit on contributions is governed by section 530A(c)(2), while after the end of the growth period, the limit on contributions is governed by section 408(a)(1).

The written governing instrument of the Trump account may provide that, immediately after the growth period, all of the assets of the Trump account will be transferred to a traditional IRA for the account beneficiary that is not a Trump account

After the growth period ... the rules under section 408 that apply to other traditional IRAs are generally applicable to Trump accounts, except as provided in section 530A(h). ... after the growth period, an unfunded Trump account that is not an auto account may be closed by the trustee if provided by the terms of the written governing instrument.

authority.source: CC-00226466-26, proposed rule withdrawing REG-117270-25, 30 Sep 2026
authority.quote: the Treasury Department and the IRS are withdrawing the prior s.1.530A-1 NPRM and issuing these proposed regulations.
This is a deviation from the standard pro-rata aggregation rule for IRAs and is preserved on Roth conversion ... A move into a non-Trump Traditional IRA ... ends this special separation.
Starting in the year the beneficiary turns 18, the contribution limit for standard IRAs applies ($7,500 in 2026)
Notice 2025-68 confirms Trump Accounts are not aggregated with other IRAs for basis allocation purposes

verdict_reason: s.530A(h)(4) has no age limit, Notice 2025-68 says the separation holds 'at all times' and that post-18 contributions follow s.408(a)(1), the closed-gap edit removes the plan without moving any baseline, and the kernel replays agree; but the +$3,500 is a 25% valuation premium that is zero under four ordinary changes of fact, the search itself is two hand-entered moves, and Treasury has reserved further guidance on exactly this treatment.
